LESSON: HEALING OF THE PARALYTIC

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Miracles of Jesus Christ
Topic 3.3: Healing of the Paralytic

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Healing of the Paralytic. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How does the healing of the paralytic build your faith in God?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the healing of the paralytic
2. apply lessons learnt from the miracle in daily life
3. appreciate God’s power over sickness and disease

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: HEALING OF THE PARALYTIC
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Healing of the Paralytic helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: HEALING OF THE PARALYTIC
Study Healing of the Paralytic like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe the healing of the paralytic

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the healing of the paralytic. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the healing of the paralytic.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Healing of the Paralytic” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the healing of the paralytic. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply lessons learnt from the miracle in daily life

What this means
In this part you learn to apply lessons learnt from the miracle in daily life. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply lessons learnt from the miracle in daily life.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Healing of the Paralytic in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply lessons learnt from the miracle in daily life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate God’s power over sickness and disease

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate God’s power over sickness and disease. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate God’s power over sickness and disease.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate God’s power over sickness and disease. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Healing of the Paralytic is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Healing of the Paralytic” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe the healing of the paralytic)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Healing of the Paralytic in your own words. (skill: apply lessons learnt from the miracle in daily life)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: appreciate God’s power over sickness and disease)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Healing of the Paralytic to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the healing of the paralytic.
3. Practise this skill: apply lessons learnt from the miracle in daily life.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate God’s power over sickness and disease.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Healing of the Paralytic from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Healing of the Paralytic: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Healing of the Paralytic?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does the healing of the paralytic build your faith in God?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Healing of the Paralytic means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the healing of the paralytic.
5. Be able to: apply lessons learnt from the miracle in daily life.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
